title: The Hoopoe, the Queen of Sheba, and a Letter

paragraphs.text: Solomon checked on the birds and noticed that the hoopoe was missing. He said he would punish the bird severely unless it brought a clear excuse. The hoopoe returned and said that it knew something Solomon did not know. It had come from Sheba with certain news. A woman was ruling the people there, and she had been given plenty of everything, including a great throne. However, she and her people were bowing down to the sun instead of Allah. Satan had made their deeds seem good to them and turned them away from the right path. They did not bow to Allah, who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and who knows what people hide and what they show. There is no deity except Him, Lord of the Great Throne.

Solomon said he would find out whether the hoopoe was telling the truth. He gave it a letter to deliver to them and told it to watch for their answer. The queen told her chiefs that a noble letter had reached her. It was from Solomon, and it began, "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful." It told them not to be proud, but to come to him in submission.

The queen asked her chiefs for advice, because she did not decide any matter without them. They answered that they were strong and ready for war, although the final command was hers. She said that when kings enter a city, they ruin it and humble its honored people. So she decided to send a gift instead and wait for the reply. When her messengers arrived, Solomon said that what Allah had given him was better than their wealth, and that it was they who were delighted with their gift.

hardWords.m: a reason given for not doing something
the special chair of a king or queen
to take something to a person
